source.author: verg
source.text: Nunc media Aenean secum per moenia ducit, Sidoniasque ostentat opes urbemque paratam; incipit effari, mediaque in voce resistit; nunc eadem labente die convivia quaerit, Iliacosque iterum demens audire labores exposcit, pendetque iterum narrantis ab ore.
source.text_original: Nunc media Aenean secum per moenia ducit, / Sidoniasque ostentat opes urbemque paratam; / incipit effari, mediaque in voce resistit; / nunc eadem labente die convivia quaerit, / Iliacosque iterum demens audire labores / exposcit, pendetque iterum narrantis ab ore.
source.text_english: Now she leads Aeneas with her through the city walls, and displays the wealth of Sidon and the city prepared for him; she begins to speak, and breaks off in mid-utterance; now, as the day wanes, she seeks the banquet, and, mad with longing, again demands to hear of the labors of Ilium, and once more hangs upon the speaker’s lips.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: pervigil Arcadio Tiphys pendebat ab astro Hagniades, felix stellis qui segnibus usum et dedit aequoreos caelo duce tendere cursus.
reuse.text_original: pervigil Arcadio Tiphys pendebat ab astro / Hagniades, felix stellis qui segnibus usum / et dedit aequoreos caelo duce tendere cursus.
reuse.text_english: All night long, Arcadian Tiphys hung poised beneath the star of the son of Hagnias, fortunate because the sluggish stars granted him their use and, with the sky as guide, set him to steer his sea-routes across the deep.
